newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs test supervisor of disputed Bosnia town.
newsitem.headline: Serbs test supervisor of disputed Bosnia town.

text.p: The American supervisor of the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko accused Serbs on Friday of organising attacks on Moslem civilians trying to visit his office in the northern river port.
U.S. diplomat Robert Farrand called for a U.N. and Bosnian Serb police investigation of the stoning of two Moslem buses on Thursday when four people were hurt as police stood by.
Farrand, who took office recently, said he would take action after receiving reports on what happened as diplomats warned that he was being tested by the Serbs.
Serbs took military control of Brcko, which had a pre-war Moslem-Croat majority, in 1992 and its future ownership was left to international arbitatration by the 1995 Bosnia peace agreement.
The Moslem visit to his office had been agreed in advance by Serb authorities who regard Brcko as an essential link between Serb territories in east and west Bosnia.
"This is a test for Farrand. For him to prove his credibility, he must ensure that those named in the U.N. report are dismissed," a Western diplomat told Reuters.
Colum Murphy, a spokesman for the international High representative in Bosnia, said Farrand had power to take action and added: "I think you will see a tough stance from him."

A U.N. police spokesman said that when the buses arrived at the supervisor's office in the centre of the town, a crowd of Serbs began assembling and shouting insults. The buses were stoned several times.
"The Serbs definitely had more than enough time to prepare for the visit," Alex Ivanko said. "That is why it is extremely suprising not to have prepared for such a small-scale visit."
Farrand's supervision is to end with a final decision on the status in March 1998.
"This is also a test for the Serb police and authorities and their ability to cooperate in Brcko," a diplomat said.
